findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the reserved-key handling for Data Center: _translate_create_fields is a pass-through negation, so the DC create step must POP/exclude `_bridge_target_project` (e.g. add it to a drop set or pop it after reading) so it is not splatted into create_issue(**fields); the plan's 'ignored by field translation' claim is only true for Cloud.
evidence: Plan quote: 'The reserved key is not a Jira field name, so it is ignored by field translation and never sent to the tracker.'

_issues.py:109-113 builds fields via `{name: value for name, value in ticket_data.items() if name not in _BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS and name not in _UNSETTABLE_AT_CREATE_FIELDS}` — a pass-through negation, not an allowlist.
_issues.py:29 `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS = frozenset({'title','ticket_type'})` — does NOT include `_bridge_target_project`.

_issues.py:188 `_with_connection_retry(lambda: self._client.create_issue(**fields))` — splats fields to Jira; an unrecognised field id triggers the HTTP 400 class documented at lines 172-177 (bug 18a5).
Contrast: Cloud AcliClient.create_issue (acli.py:274-330) EXTRACTS named fields and ignores the rest (docstring lines 170-171), so the 'ignored' claim holds ONLY for Cloud.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the reserved key _bridge_target_project 'is ignored by field translation and never sent to the tracker', but the Data Center _translate_create_fields passes through every key not in {'title','ticket_type'} or the unsettable set, so the reserved key would be splatted into self._client.create_issue(**fields) and sent to Jira as a field id.
findings.location: Approach — 'Create targets the ticket's resolved project' (reserved-key sentence); src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:100-151,186-188
scenarios: A ticket resolving to project B on the Data Center transport: the create payload carries _bridge_target_project, _translate_create_fields keeps it, and create_issue(**fields) sends it to Jira — rejected as an unknown field, aborting the create.
findings.suggested_fix: In the DC create step, read `project = ticket_data.get('_bridge_target_project') or self.project`, then ensure the reserved key is removed before/inside _translate_create_fields (add it to _BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS or pop it), so `fields` never carries it into self._client.create_issue(**fields).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the Data Center transport must DROP `_bridge_target_project` from the payload before sending (e.g. add it to `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS` or pop it inside `create_issue`), since `_translate_create_fields` is a denylist passthrough that otherwise forwards the reserved key to Jira REST as an unknown field and triggers HTTP 400.
evidence: Plan: 'The reserved key is not a Jira field name, so it is ignored by field translation and never sent to the tracker.'
_issues.py:109-113 keeps `name not in _BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS and name not in _UNSETTABLE_AT_CREATE_FIELDS` — a denylist, not an allowlist
_issues.py:29 `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS = frozenset({'title', 'ticket_type'})` — does not include `_bridge_target_project`
_issues.py:186-188: `fields = _translate_create_fields(ticket_data); fields.setdefault('project', ...); self._client.create_issue(**fields)` — leaked key reaches the REST call
_issues.py:171-177 docstring: splatting rebar's own field names into create got 'the entire request rejected — HTTP 400 … Field … cannot be set'
findings.finding: The plan asserts the reserved `_bridge_target_project` key 'is ignored by field translation and never sent to the tracker', but the Data Center transport's `_translate_create_fields` is a denylist passthrough that keeps every field not in `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS={'title','ticket_type'}`/`_UNSETTABLE_AT_CREATE_FIELDS`. The unknown `_bridge_target_project` key would survive translation and be splatted into `self._client.create_issue(**fields)`, sending it to Jira REST as an unknown field id and triggering the HTTP-400 rejection the method's own docstring documents.
findings.location: Approach → 'Create targets the ticket's resolved project' (last sentence); Scope → jira_datacenter/_issues.py
scenarios: A multi-project create dispatched through the Data Center transport with `_bridge_target_project` stamped into the mutation fields
findings.suggested_fix: In jira_datacenter/_issues.py, add `_bridge_target_project` to `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS` (so translation strips it) and read the value from `ticket_data` for the `project` key as the plan already shows; correct the plan's claim that the key is ignored 'by field translation' — that only holds for Cloud's explicit-extraction path.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the mapping accessor: use projects_store.load_mapping(repo_root) (returns a Mapping) for resolve_project and for the project set (mapping.projects), or state that read_projects supplies the set directly (its return IS the projects dict) — do not treat read_projects's result as a Mapping with a .projects attribute.
evidence: projects_store.py:116-118 read_projects returns load_mapping(repo_root).projects, i.e. dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
projects_store.py:97 resolve_project(ticket: dict, mapping: Mapping) expects a Mapping
projects_store.py:48 load_mapping(...) -> Mapping is the producer of a Mapping (with .projects)

Plan: 'resolve_project(ticket, mapping) ... against the store mapping (loaded once via projects_store.read_projects(repo_root))' conflates the dict return of read_projects with the Mapping resolve_project needs
findings.finding: The plan uses read_projects to obtain the mapping fed to resolve_project and to read mapping.projects, but read_projects returns the projects dict (dict[str, dict]) — not a Mapping; resolve_project(ticket, mapping) requires a Mapping and mapping.projects is only an attribute of the Mapping object produced by load_mapping.
findings.location: Approach 'loaded once via projects_store.read_projects(repo_root)' and 'read_projects(repo_root) (keys of mapping.projects)'
scenarios: Differ passes read_projects() output (a dict) into resolve_project, which expects a Mapping; applier reads .projects off read_projects() output, which is already the projects dict with no .projects attribute
findings.suggested_fix: Use load_mapping(repo_root) to obtain the Mapping for resolve_project and mapping.projects; if the guard caller only needs the key set, use set(read_projects(repo_root)) directly instead of read_projects(...).projects.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the `_bridge_target_project` reserved-key contract durably (a shared named constant referenced by all transports, or a one-line note in the module/adapter docstring) so future transports honour it.
evidence: The key is a new implicit contract spanning outbound_differ.py, acli.py, and _issues.py
No mention of defining it as a named constant or noting it in AGENTS.md/a docstring so future adapters honour it
Mitigating: the stated fallback ('or self.jira_project' / 'or self.project') means an adapter that ignores the key degrades to single-project rather than breaking dangerously
findings.finding: The new cross-component contract — the reserved payload key `_bridge_target_project` that flows from `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` into both transports — is described in the approach prose but not captured as a shared constant or documented decision, so a future third transport (or field-translation change) could silently omit reading it.
findings.location: Approach — 'stamped into the mutation's fields under the reserved key _bridge_target_project'
scenarios: A future adapter author adds a third TicketTransport and does not know to read _bridge_target_project, silently reverting to single-project creates
findings.suggested_fix: Define `_bridge_target_project` as a single module-level constant imported by the differ and both adapters, and add a brief docstring note that any TicketTransport.create_issue must honour it (falling back to its construction-time project).
